https://english.radio.cz/hundreds-police.text: CS DE EN ES FR РУ УК Hundreds of police officers and a helicopter to monitor Prague Pride march Facebook Twitter Police will step up security at all accompanying events of the Prague Pride festival, which begins in Prague on Monday. Several hundred police officers will be deployed for the Pride march, which will culminate the festival the following Saturday. They will secure the entire route from Wenceslas Square to Střelecký Island, while a police helicopter will monitor the area from the air. Traffic in the city centre will be restricted on the day of the march. According to police spokesperson Eva Kropáčová, the security measures were adopted in light of recent risk assessments, including the recent attack on a similar event in Berlin. Russian missiles spark huge factory fires in Ukraine’s Odesa and Zaporizhzhia Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 16/10/2026 - 14:46 GMT+2 Russian strikes ignited massive fires at businesses in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia as President Zelensky met European leaders for talks. … More Russian strikes sparked major fires in Ukraine's Odesa and Zaporizhzhia regions on Friday 16 October , leaving industrial premises engulfed in flames . ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT In Odesa, firefighters battled a blaze at a factory producing household goods , dragging hoses towards the burning building as products lay scattered across the ground. Further east, in Zaporizhzhia, emergency crews used an elevated platform to tackle a fire covering 500 square metres at a private business . Footage released by Ukraine's emergency services shows firefighters directing jets of water into the flames at both sites. The attacks came as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky joined European leaders for talks. Separate footage shows him arriving alongside European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa . German Chancellor Friedrich Merz , Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk were also among the leaders filmed at the gathering. The scenes underline the continuing impact of Russian strikes on Ukrainian businesses as Kyiv pursues diplomatic discussions with its European partners .
